title: IIT Bombay Student Reps Seek Systemic Reforms, Clarify Stance on Professor
excerpt: In an official statement, IIT Bombay student representatives said their protest sought institutional reforms and accountability after the death of Sahil Wakode — not a defence of cheating — and clarified they have never presumed guilt of Prof. Suryanarayana Doolla.
body:
• Student representatives clarified that the campus protests were aimed at systemic reforms and institutional accountability, not at defending cheating or academic misconduct.
  • The students said they have never presumed guilt of Prof. Suryanarayana Doolla and continue to support him as a member of the faculty.
  • Their demand that Doolla be relieved of his administrative duties as Dean of Administrative Affairs was a precautionary step to keep the investigation independent, they said.
  • An open-house session with Director Shireesh Kedare produced commitments on actionable timelines for an 18-point charter of reform demands.

Student representatives at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay have issued an official statement clarifying the purpose of recent campus protests following the death of second-year BTech student Sahil Wakode, saying the agitation was driven by demands for systemic reforms and accountability, not by any attempt to condone academic misconduct.

The statement, reported by news agency ANI, is the clearest articulation yet of the student body's position in a case that has drawn national attention. The representatives said they do not support cheating in any form, and that the protests were intended to highlight long-standing institutional concerns and press the administration for structural changes that could prevent similar tragedies.

Clarifying the stance on Prof. Doolla

Addressing the case of Professor Suryanarayana Doolla, who was the course invigilator during the examination at the center of the controversy, the student representatives said their position has never been one of presuming guilt or prejudging the ongoing investigation.

"We stand with Professor Doolla as a member of our faculty community and believe that the investigation must be allowed to proceed fairly and impartially."

— Student representatives, IIT Bombay

The representatives explained that their demand for Doolla to be relieved of his administrative duties as Dean of Administrative Affairs was strictly precautionary, intended to ensure that the legal and institutional probes remain independent and free of administrative influence. Doolla has been relieved of the deanship and continues to serve as a professor at the institute; the IIT Bombay Faculty Forum has described him as a professor in good standing.

The Faculty Forum has staged a march in support of Doolla, and its president, Professor Rajkumar S Pant, said the professor had been discharging his duties according to institute procedures.

Background of the case

Wakode, a 20-year-old student, died on September 18. His death followed an examination-related incident shortly before, after which the institute issued a statement describing him as having been caught using a phone during the exam and alleging he had uploaded the question paper to ChatGPT. The institute later apologised for its earlier communication and retracted its characterisations of the circumstances before the investigation was completed.

An abetment case has been filed against Doolla in connection with the death, and the investigation has been transferred to the Mumbai Police Crime Branch, which is continuing its inquiry.

Reforms and next steps

Student representatives submitted an 18-point charter of demands to the administration, covering reforms to disciplinary procedures, improved grievance mechanisms, stronger counselling and mental-health support, and greater student participation in institutional processes.

Following an open-house session with Director Shireesh Kedare and other members of the administration, officials acknowledged the charter and committed to actionable timelines for systemic reform. The representatives said they appreciated the director's engagement with the student community and his approach to identifying and addressing institutional issues that had come to light.

The representatives also pushed back against external organizations attempting to frame the event through outside political lenses.

"The loss of Sahil should not become a platform for external political interests, organisations, or narratives to shape the concerns of the IIT Bombay student community."

— Student representatives, IIT Bombay
The statement reiterated that all concerns, demands and reform measures must remain student-led, transparent and rooted within the institute's community.

The representatives said they would continue to seek accountability, transparency and institutional reform while working with the institute, even as the investigation into the circumstances of Wakode's death continues.
